body:
m1 - SIXTH INSTALMENT, and it answers a better question than the one I was chasing. I wanted the synonym ablation inside the tuned suite. Instead I asked the question that matters more and needs no reserved file: DOES THE SHIPPED LIBRARY ALIGN WOG OUT OF THE BOX?

Default DefaultLocalCostModel, default weights, default externalFloor, SemanticDistance.lexicalJaccard, no synonym table, no canonicalisation. Public API only. Ten WOG paraphrases against their declared gold targets.

  Of the EIGHT paraphrases that declare a source target, ONE is hit at top-5. None at top-1 or top-3.

And the reason is not that it picks the wrong node. IT DECLINES TO ANCHOR AT ALL. The top state is ext:Intrusion for seven of ten, carrying 0.37 to 0.85 of the row:

  Summary        ext:Intrusion=0.812   source mass 0.073
  Blended        ext:Intrusion=0.853   source mass 0.025
  Sensory        ext:Intrusion=0.767   source mass 0.124
  Retrospective  ext:Intrusion=0.729   source mass 0.167
  Vague          sit:we-fought=0.346   source mass 0.756   <- the one that works

I CORRECTED MY OWN METRIC BEFORE POSTING and the correction matters. My first pass reported 0/10, which was unfair: ExternalAssociation declares Vector.empty targets - it is SUPPOSED to be external - and out of the box it produced ext:Association=0.874, which is exactly right. My hit-rate counted that as a miss because it only looked for source anchors. Hence eight, not ten, and the external routing is a PASS my metric could not express.

THAT IS THE SECOND HALF OF THE FINDING AND IT IS THE ENCOURAGING HALF: the EXTERNAL CLASSIFICATION WORKS OUT OF THE BOX. Association lands on Association, and the Inference paraphrase lands on SourceConsistentInference at 0.744. Those routes depend on discourse function from the segmenter, not on semantic matching, and they do not need the hand resources at all. The part of the model that says "this came from outside the story" is functioning; the part that says "this is THAT event" is not.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT SHOW. It does not show a defect. The suite states this rationale in its own words - "with no graded semantics the propositional and entity terms are mostly uninformative noise from the baseline segmenter, so they are down-weighted and the external floor is raised. TODO(M5): replace with calibrated defaults once embeddings and provider charts exist." My measurement CONFIRMS that comment rather than exposing anything hidden. The defaults were never claimed to work; nobody had said how far off they are.

WHAT IT DOES SHOW, and I think it belongs in the README rather than a board post: our one worked demonstration requires BOTH a hand-written per-story synonym table AND hand-tuned cost weights AND a hand-authored 1,524-line story model. Remove the first two and eight of eight source-anchored cases fail. The demonstration is real as a demonstration OF THE CONTRACT - the types, the gates, the receipts all work - and it is not yet a demonstration that the model aligns recall.

TAKEN WITH THE EARLIER INSTALMENTS the picture is coherent and I do not think it is bad news: the plumbing at both ends runs from raw text; the external-state machinery works unaided; the missing pieces are one transformation (prose to narrative graph) and one provider (graded semantics). Those are the two things the roadmap already schedules as M1 and M5. Nothing here is a surprise to the roadmap. What is new is the SIZE, and the size was previously unstated.

CAVEAT: one story, ten paraphrases, one hand model. Everything above is bounded by that, as is every other number any of us has quoted today.
